thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLA breach detected for tenant=\"LuminaCare\" check=\"tenant-response-latency\" severity=critical — P99 latency 2.4s (SLO 1.0s). paging: eng-oncall
Amelia: ack. I'm on it, paging Sanjay now. if this is widespread let's start degraded-mode routing.
Amelia: @Sanjay can you grab this? looks like a tenant-specific latency spike on embed endpoints.
Sanjay: on it. pulling traces now. could be KV cache thrash or model variant fallback.
Sanjay: running `rbx traces --tenant LuminaCare --query "latency > 1000" --window 5m` to get call sites.
opsbot: deploy-bot noticed a small model rollout 3m ago: model-id=redwood-v2-optimized, rollout=5% (service=embed-gw). link: <https://redwood.internal/deploys/rollouts/4621>
Amelia: hmm that rollout might correlate. Sanjay, if the rollout is causing mis-routing we should pause it.
Sanjay: pausing rollout now -> `deployctl pause 4621`
Sanjay: paused. telemetry still shows elevated latency for LuminaCare only.
Amelia: can we reduce page noise — set non-critical checks to warning for that tenant while we investigate? want to avoid paging other teams.
Marta: +1. I can flip the check to warning for LuminaCare in the checks config.
Marta: editing check: `checks/tenant-response-latency` -> add `ignore_for_tenant: LuminaCare` for severity=page. applying patch...
Marta: ```yaml
# patch applied
- check: tenant-response-latency
  threshold_p99_ms: 1000
  severity: page
+ check: tenant-response-latency
  threshold_p99_ms: 2000
  severity: warning
  tenant_overrides:
    LuminaCare:
      threshold_p99_ms: 2500
      severity: warning
```
Amelia: :white_check_mark: temporary suppression in place. This prevents repeat paging while we root cause. Keep an eye on customer impact though.
Luis: looping in infra — could be a noisy tenant causing node contention on embedding workers. @infra please check GPU utilization on pool embed-pool-3.
opsbot: infra-alert: embed-pool-3 GPU utilization spike 95% across nodes; top processes: model-server (LuminaCare sessions).
Sanjay: GPU saturation confirmed. LuminaCare has a small traffic burst of long sequences. We should throttle sequence length server-side for that tenant as short-term mitigation.
Sanjay: Applying sequence cap via config flag for tenant: `max_seq_len: 512` -> `configs/tenants/LuminaCare.json`
Sanjay: ```json
{ "tenant": "LuminaCare", "runtime_overrides": { "max_seq_len": 512, "concurrency_limit": 8 } }
```
Marta: applied. patch rolled through. monitoring metrics for p99 latency and token throughput.
Amelia: customer-facing note: Ops — prepare a targeted message to LuminaCare support saying we've mitigated sudden latency by applying temporary limits and paused an internal rollout. ETA for full resolution ~2h.
Marta: drafting message and opening incident ticket CT-1024. assigning owner Sanjay. link: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/CT-1024>
Sanjay: collecting detailed traces to find whether cache churn or specific request patterns cause long sequences. early sign: 60% of heavy sessions are from a specific client id: app-client-xy.
Amelia: can we add a dashboard tile and quick filter for LuminaCare + client id so oncall can triage faster?
Luis: I'll add a dashboard now on the oncall panel: /dash create "LuminaCare - Live SLOs" with panels: p99 latency, GPU util, queue depth, top client ids.
Luis: dashboard created: <https://redwood.internal/dashboards/6482>
Amelia: nice. add an auto-refresh 10s and a note to the top explaining the temporary config changes.
Luis: done. also created an alert targeting PS-only (no pages) for GPU util > 90% so infra gets visibility without paging SRE.
Marta: reminder — we still need to tune check thresholds post-incident. I'll create a follow-up story in ENG-OPS to adjust tenant-specific thresholds and add rate-based dampening for small bursts.
Marta: creating ticket ENGOPS-529 with acceptance criteria: 1) tenant override table for p95/p99 thresholds, 2) per-tenant sequence caps optional flag, 3) dashboard template, 4) postmortem summary.
Sanjay: telemetry shows p99 dropped from 2.4s to 0.9s after sequence cap and rollout pause. looks stable for now.
Amelia: handing off to Luis for overnight watch. summary: paused rollout 4621, temporary tenant caps applied (max_seq_len=512, concurrency=8), dashboard + ticket created, LuminaCare notified. CT-1024 created.
Amelia: @Luis you're up — please escalate if we see p99 > 1.2s again or GPU util > 92%.
Luis: taking watch. I'll keep the dashboard on rotation and check-in in 30m.
opsbot: incident-bot: Escalation policy set to "oncall -> infra" for this incident.
Luis: quick note for oncall handoff later — we should add a playbook step to silence tenant noise for short windows instead of full page threshold changes. adding to ENGOPS-529.
Marta: agreed. also suggesting a preflight check before rollouts for high-cost tenants: simulate 5% traffic in canary against known heavy sequences.
Amelia: excellent. postmortem owners: Sanjay (investigate root cause), Marta (alert/threshold changes), Luis (dashboard + playbook). I'll schedule a 1hr retro tomorrow.
Sanjay: one more thing — we should consider soft-fallback to cheaper model variant for that tenant when GPU saturation is high. raising a feature request in model-ops.
Luis: noted. I'll include a section in ENGOPS-529 about model-variant fallback and cost/latency tradeoffs.
Amelia: thanks team. marking this thread as monitored. will update CT-1024 when we have root-cause. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: note: incident CT-1024 updated -> status=monitoring, owner=Sanjay, impact=tenant-limited.
Luis: closing my watch for now, will re-open if thresholds cross.
Amelia: closing thread — follow-up meeting scheduled: 2026-03-16 10:00 UTC.
notes: Tenant-specific SLA alert surfaced due to GPU saturation during small rollout; immediate mitigations included pausing rollout, tenant runtime caps, temporary check severity downgrade, dashboard creation, and a follow-up ticket for alert tuning and playbook updates.
